findings.title: Route-scoped radar rankings consume unfiltered runtime events
findings.what: The component derives route-scoped timelines, token data, tool data, and API errors, but builds runtimeById directly from the complete runtimeEvents prop. A date-filtered partial session can therefore receive full-session runtime evidence in computeSessionScorecard, changing its radar composite and top/bottom ranking with evidence outside the displayed scope. Project or mode filters can likewise admit runtime data without applying the same predicate used for the other inputs.
findings.fix: Derive a route-scoped runtime-events collection using the same supported project/date/mode semantics before building runtimeById, or omit runtimeEvents from a scorecard whenever the selected scope cannot be reproduced at runtime-event granularity.
findings.acceptance: Add a component regression fixture containing one session with in-scope timeline/token/tool data and runtime events split across an included and excluded date; verify that changing only excluded runtime evidence does not change the displayed route-scoped radar score or rank. Repeat for every route dimension the runtime-event shape supports.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed that lines 762-777 explicitly scope every other scorecard input, while line 820 maps raw runtimeEvents and line 836 passes that unfiltered record into the scorecard. The finding is limited to this reproducible scope mismatch and does not assume a defect in the imported scorecard implementation.

findings.title: Polling permits overlapping status requests
findings.what: tick awaits fetchRemoteSessions, but setInterval invokes tick every four seconds independently of whether an earlier invocation has settled. If requests take longer than the interval or stall, concurrent requests accumulate, increasing browser, server, and cluster-status load and permitting older responses to overwrite newer state.
findings.fix: Use a self-scheduling timeout started in tick's finally block, or guard tick with an in-flight flag/AbortController so at most one polling request exists and cancel it during cleanup.
findings.acceptance: With fetchRemoteSessions held pending across multiple four-second clock advances, verify it is called only once; after resolving it, verify exactly one later poll is scheduled, and verify unmount aborts or prevents further polling and state updates.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed there is no in-flight guard or request abort: line 73 awaits the request, while line 80 independently schedules repeated tick calls. The cleanup flag suppresses state updates after unmount but does not cancel or serialize requests.
